# ak-ui-react

> React port of [ak-ui](https://github.com/YunYouJun/ak-ui) and [prts-design](https://github.com/MooncellWiki/prts-design) — an Arknights-inspired industrial / tactical terminal design system for React.
> Framework-agnostic SCSS and DOM controllers are vendored from upstream; components are implemented in modern React (18 & 19).

Package: `@swufefox/ak-ui-react`
- Repository: https://github.com/SwufeFox/ak-ui-react
- Showcase: https://ak-ui-react.pages.dev
- **API reference — authoritative prop tables**: [`docs/api.md`](./docs/api.md) · https://github.com/SwufeFox/ak-ui-react/blob/master/docs/api.md
- **Stylesheet**: `@swufefox/ak-ui-react/style.css`
- **Peer dependencies**: `react >= 18` and `react-dom >= 18`. There is no runtime dependency beyond these two.
- **Client boundary**: the package entry is marked `'use client'`, so every component renders on the client. Importing it from a Next.js server component is safe; the DOM controllers under `@swufefox/ak-ui-react/core` have no React dependency and stay server-usable.
- **Fonts**: Chakra Petch and Oswald (OFL-1.1) ship with the package and cover the label and display roles. The game's own Bender / Novecento Sans Wide are not redistributed but stay first in the font stacks.

---

## 0. What to read, and where

| File | Contains |
| :--- | :--- |
| `llms.txt` (this file) | The design contract, the component index, usage patterns, token and motion rules |
| [`docs/api.md`](./docs/api.md) | Every public component and hook, with each prop, variant and method documented — generated from the emitted `.d.ts` JSDoc, so it is never out of date |
| `AGENTS.md` | The contributor guide: architecture, build stages and the conventions a change must follow |

Read `docs/api.md` for exact prop names, types and defaults; read this file for the rules that
decide *how* to use them.

---

## 1. Quick Start

### Installation

```bash
npm install @swufefox/ak-ui-react
# or
pnpm add @swufefox/ak-ui-react
# or
bun add @swufefox/ak-ui-react
```

### Import Stylesheet

Import the stylesheet once at your app's root entry file (`main.tsx` or `App.tsx`):

```tsx
import '@swufefox/ak-ui-react/style.css'
```

---

## 2. The ak-ui design contract

ak-ui is an original design language inspired by the information hierarchy, industrial geometry and
tactical-terminal atmosphere of Arknights interfaces. It ships reusable constraints for independent
products; it does not aim to reproduce a specific game screen, composition, brand or asset. Judge a
result by conformance to this contract, not by similarity to a screenshot.

This section is the React port of the upstream ak-ui skill (`skills/ak-ui/SKILL.md` and its
`references/`) together with the prts-design porting rules. The authoritative prop tables live in
[`docs/api.md`](./docs/api.md).

### 2.1 Style intensity

| Mode | Use when | What it changes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `accent` | The host already has a brand and a layout | Keep the layout; add ak-ui typography, signal colours, visible focus and compact metadata. At most one restrained cut or line treatment per component. |
| `system` | Backends, tooling, web apps (the default) | The full component language: layered neutral surfaces, asymmetric emphasis, clipped geometry, dense but legible metadata, functional signals, decisive feedback. |
| `terminal` | Immersive landing pages and showcases | Adds command planes, telemetry, perspective, parallax and staged motion — only where the content benefits. Recompose for mobile instead of shrinking a desktop control room. |

Intensity is not a light/dark switch. This package ships the terminal-forward styling and lets a
host dial it back by not using the immersive pieces (`AkDepth`, `AkParticleField`,
`AkLoadingScreen`, `AkScreen`, the `/core` site controllers).

### 2.2 Principles

1. **Build hierarchy before decoration.** Every surface needs one dominant command or value, supporting context and quiet metadata. Vary size, weight, contrast, alignment and whitespace before adding borders or glow. Short labels, identifiers, counts, timestamps, progress and state text must carry real information — never add meaningless serial numbers for atmosphere.
2. **Use asymmetric, purposeful geometry.** Prefer rectangular modules, clipped corners, offset rules, stepped edges or one slanted axis. Rounded cards, uniform pill shapes, soft floating shadows and evenly spaced dashboard tiles must not dominate. The hit area stays rectangular and large enough even when the visible shape is clipped (`AkCut`, `AkBrackets`, `AkCorner`).
3. **Treat colour as a signal.** Build most surfaces from paper, graphite, black, white and muted grey. Reserve cyan/blue for information, yellow for action or warning, orange for concentrated emphasis, green for success and red for danger. Pair every colour change with a label, icon, pattern or geometry change — colour is never the only indicator. Glow is local feedback, not a permanent background effect.
4. **Make typography carry structure.** `--ak-font-command` (serif) for major Chinese command labels, `--ak-font-sans` for prose and controls, `--ak-font-mono` for identifiers, telemetry and aligned values. Metadata may be letter-spaced (`--ak-type-wide`); do not uppercase, italicise and monospace every line. Bilingual pairs use `AkBilingual`, Latin display words use `AkDisplay`, aligned numbers use `AkNum`.
5. **Layer surfaces, not clutter.** Combine paper-like light surfaces and graphite dark surfaces when hierarchy requires contrast. Explain elevation with strong rules, small offsets and controlled shadows — never stack borders, gradients, noise, glow and bevels on one element.
6. **Keep interaction decisive.** Hover, press, selection, loading and focus must change at least two of signal, position, fill, line or label. Transitions stay quick and mechanical. The keyboard focus indicator must stay visible and must not be clipped away.

### 2.3 Composition rules

- Align related data to a stable grid, then break the grid only for the primary command or focal object.
- Interactive targets stay at least 24×24 CSS px in the package (primary navigation links are 44px). The upstream skill asks for 44×44 wherever the control can afford it — use 44px for primary actions in a host app.
- Preserve readable line lengths and real whitespace around primary actions.
- Recompose multi-plane terminal layouts for narrow viewports; never rely on horizontal scrolling.
- Keep overlays above transformed ancestors, and verify portalled content (Popover API, native `<dialog>`) in its real DOM position.
- Let content decide density. Consumer pages must not inherit showcase-level telemetry by default.

### 2.4 Brand adaptation

Preserve the host's intentional brand colours, typography and voice. Map them onto the semantic roles first, then apply the ak-ui geometry, hierarchy, density and feedback.

```css
.brand-console {
  --ak-font-command: var(--brand-display-font);
  --ak-signal-info: var(--brand-primary);
  --ak-signal-accent: var(--brand-accent);
  --ak-surface-canvas: var(--brand-canvas);
}
```

Do not force the default cyan/yellow palette onto a recognisable brand, and do not remap the danger,
warning, success, disabled or focus roles so aggressively that their meaning or contrast is lost.

### 2.5 Originality boundary

Use original, licensed or host-supplied imagery. The package ships no game logo, character art, UI
texture, icon, screenshot, audio or extracted asset — every icon-bearing component takes its icon
from props (`icon`, `prefixIcon`, `children`), and portraits are host-supplied with a neutral themed
placeholder. Removing the ak-ui styling must leave a recognisable host product.

### 2.6 Common failure modes

- A black background with cyan borders and indiscriminate glow.
- Every element clipped, skewed, numbered, uppercase or monospace.
- Decorative telemetry competing with real content.
- Tiny labels and controls justified as "game-like density".
- A desktop terminal scaled down until it is unusable on mobile.
- Brand colours overwritten instead of mapped to semantic roles.
- Headless behaviour replaced by hand-written interaction code for styling convenience.
- Similarity achieved by copying game assets instead of applying the contract.

### 2.7 Token contract

Semantic tokens are the only sanctioned way to express a repeated visual decision. Every one is a
`--ak-*` custom property on `:root` / `[data-ak-theme]`.

| Role | Token | Terminal | Archive |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Page canvas | `--ak-surface-canvas` | `#111315` | `#eef0f1` |
| Light paper panel | `--ak-surface-panel` | `rgba(253,253,251,.9)` | `rgba(253,253,251,.96)` |
| Quiet panel | `--ak-surface-muted` | `rgba(235,236,235,.9)` | `rgba(228,230,232,.92)` |
| Raised / dark panel | `--ak-surface-raised` | `rgba(66,66,66,.92)` | `#ffffff` |
| Sunken surface | `--ak-surface-sunken` / `--ak-surface-sunken-2` | `#1a1b1c` / `#232425` | `#fdfdfb` / `#f2f3f4` |
| Inverse surface | `--ak-surface-inverse` | `#fdfdfb` | `#1b1d1f` |
| Primary text | `--ak-text-primary` | `#f8f8f5` | `#1b1d1f` |
| Secondary text | `--ak-text-secondary` | `rgba(248,248,245,.68)` | `rgba(27,29,31,.68)` |
| Text on light surfaces | `--ak-text-inverse` | `#1b1d1f` | `#f8f8f5` |
| Information | `--ak-signal-info` | `#18d1ff` | `#0098dc` |
| Action / warning | `--ak-signal-action` | `#ffd800` | `#c99d00` |
| Concentrated accent | `--ak-signal-accent` | `--ak-color-accent` (`#f6540e`) | same |
| Success | `--ak-signal-success` | `#46c47c` | same |
| Danger | `--ak-signal-danger` | `#e33b3b` | same |
| Disabled | `--ak-signal-disabled` | `--ak-color-low` | same |

Raw palette values are exposed as `--ak-color-*` (`white`, `black`, `blue`, `yellow`, `dark-blue`,
`light-blue`, `gray`, `dark`, `low`, `basic`, `primary`, `secondary`, `advanced`, `accent`) — use
them to define or inspect raw values, never in component rules.

Other token families:

- **Typography** — `--ak-font-sans`, `--ak-font-serif`, `--ak-font-mono`, `--ak-font-command`; `--ak-type-display-size`, `--ak-type-title-size`, `--ak-type-label-size`, `--ak-type-data-size`, `--ak-type-tight`, `--ak-type-wide`.
- **Spacing & density** — `--ak-space-1` … `--ak-space-6`, `--ak-density-control-height`, `--ak-density-panel-padding`; runtime knobs `--ak-density-scale` / `--ak-density-control`.
- **Geometry & depth** — `--ak-line-hairline`, `--ak-line-strong`, `--ak-cut-sm` / `--ak-cut-md` / `--ak-cut-lg`, `--ak-radius-subtle`, `--ak-shadow-panel` / `-card` / `-subtle` / `-elevated` / `-signal` / `-neon`, `--ak-depth-perspective`.
- **Motion & focus** — `--ak-motion-fast` (120ms), `--ak-motion-base` (200ms), `--ak-motion-slow` (420ms), `--ak-ease-standard`, `--ak-ease-emphasized`, `--ak-ease-tactical`, `--ak-ease-snap`, `--ak-focus-color`, `--ak-focus-width`, `--ak-focus-offset`.
- **Arknights data palettes** — `--ak-rarity-1` … `--ak-rarity-6` (with `-text` variants), `--ak-prof-*` (eight professions), `--ak-role-*` (eight combat roles), `--ak-terminal-paper` / `-muted` / `-dark` / `-cyan` / `-accent`.

Rules: do not hard-code a repeated decision that a public token covers; do not redefine a public
`--ak-*` token to mean a different role; prefer scoped overrides over changing `:root` for one
feature; keep a fallback on every `var(--ak-…)` so consumer overrides keep working.

### 2.8 Three orthogonal knobs

Geometry is never welded into a rule. Every interactive component reads its size from a CSS custom property, so there are three ways to adjust it without writing CSS:

**a. `size` prop — per-instance tier** (`'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'`, default `'md'` = the pre-tuning look):
```tsx
<AkButton size="sm">Compact</AkButton>
<AkTable size="lg" columns={columns} rows={rows} />
```
Supported on: `AkButton`, `AkCard`, `AkStatus`, `AkTag`, `AkNotice`, `AkField`, `AkInput`, `AkTextarea`, `AkSelect`, `AkChoice`, `AkInputNumber`, `AkProgress`, `AkGauge`, `AkSlider`, `AkTable`, `AkDialog`, `AkTabs`, `AkSegmented`, `AkPagination`, `AkItem`, `AkSlot`, `AkSearch`, `AkDropdownMenu`, `AkContextMenu`, `AkPopover`.

**b. `tokens` prop — per-instance CSS-variable override** (any `--ak-*` the component actually reads):
```tsx
<AkButton tokens={{ '--ak-button-bg': '#ff5e19', '--ak-button-height': '2rem' }} />
<AkDialog tokens={{ '--ak-dialog-w': '52rem' }} open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} />
```
Keys that are *functional state* (e.g. `--ak-progress-value`) are owned by the component and are not overridable. `tokens` is written into the inline `style`, so an explicit `style` prop still wins.

**c. `data-ak-density` — subtree density scale** (`'compact' | 'cozy' | 'spacious'`, default `cozy`):
```tsx
<div data-ak-density="compact">{/* controls, tables and fields inside all shrink 12.5% */}</div>
```
Density multiplies control heights and spacing via `--ak-density-scale` / `--ak-density-control`; it never changes colour or layout direction.

### 2.9 Motion & lifecycle

The defaults below are implementation choices of this library, not measurements of the game's animation timeline.

| Effect | API | Defaults |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Entrance | `createEntrance` (`…/core/effects`), `AkEntrance` | 650ms, delay 0, distance 24px, direction `up`, easing `cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)`; animates opacity + CSS `translate`, never overwrites `transform` |
| Count-up | `createCountUp`, `AkCountUp` | 1000ms, delay 0, from 0, cubic ease-out; the callback owns the formatting |
| Pointer depth | `createDashboardDepth` (`…/core/depth`), `AkDepth` | `[data-depth]` layers, maxX 130, maxY 70, writes `--ak-layer-x` / `--ak-layer-y` |
| Section navigation | `createSectionNavigation`, `AkSectionNavigator` | 650ms transition, 420ms section entrance, 20px displacement |
| Media gallery | `createMediaGallery`, `AkMediaGallery` | 420ms slide, loops by default |
| Mobile menu | `createMobileMenu`, `AkMobileMenu` | 200ms entrance, 70ms stagger, 24px displacement |
| Asset loader | `createAssetLoader`, `AkAssetLoader` | real task completion, error/retry, cancellation; progress counts settled tasks, not bytes |
| Particle field | `createParticleField`, `AkParticleField` | 360 particles, `grid` / `orbit` / `wave`, WebGL → 2D → static fallback |

Lifecycle rules: creating a controller does not start it — call `play()` on the intended event.
`play()` cancels the previous animation, `cancel()` restores the visible state, and `destroy()`
removes the preference listener — always destroy on unmount. Never drive the same element's
`translate` from two controllers; nest wrappers instead. Do not put a per-frame value in an
`aria-live` region: mark the interpolation `aria-hidden` and render separate static target text.
Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the entrance controller skips playback, the count-up renders
its target immediately, and CSS entrances lose their animation while staying fully visible.

### 2.10 Who owns what

| Concern | Owner |
| :--- | :--- |
| Semantics, ARIA, focus management, keyboard input | the native element or headless primitive |
| Controlled state and emitted events | your component API |
| Geometry, surfaces, typography, motion | ak-ui CSS and tokens |
| Copy, brand, information priority | the host application |

Do not replace behaviour to make styling easier — style the rendered parts and the public state
attributes (`aria-selected`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-invalid`, `data-state`). This
package already leans on platform primitives: native `<dialog>` with `showModal()`, the Popover API
for menus and popovers, roving `tabIndex` with arrow/Home/End on tablists, `aria-current="location"`
on in-page anchors.

### 2.11 Quality checklist

- The chosen intensity is evident and not exceeded; existing ak-ui primitives are reused before new lookalikes are written.
- Repeated visual decisions use public `--ak-*` tokens; brand values are mapped, not overwritten.
- The primary command or value is immediately identifiable; metadata supports real content.
- Rest, hover, active, focus-visible, open/closed, selected, disabled, invalid, loading, empty and error states are exercised — never signalled by colour alone.
- Keyboard focus is visible and unclipped; overlays close on Escape and return focus.
- Touch targets stay large enough; the layout is inspected at one desktop and one narrow viewport.
- Motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`; content stays usable without JavaScript.
- Type-check, build and a real browser pass; the console stays clean.

### 2.12 The prts-design layer

The Arknights data layers (rarity, profession, elite, potential, mastery, skill sheets, talents, modules, dossiers, voices, operator cards, stage cards, panels, feedback) are ports of [prts-design](https://github.com/MooncellWiki/prts-design) (MIT). The porting rules are part of the contract:

- Upstream class names are kept verbatim (`.ak-op-card__portrait`, `.ak-skill__icon`, `.ak-talent-table`, `.ak-voice__play`, …) so the vendored CSS stays recognisable.
- Upstream CSS variables are mapped onto `--ak-*` semantic tokens (`--ak-bg-surface` → `--ak-surface-sunken`, `--ak-fg` → `--ak-text-primary`, `--ak-accent` → `--ak-signal-info`); upstream values with no token become component-scoped custom properties.
- One rule set serves both themes — colour differences live in the tokens, never in a second theme branch.
- No game artwork ships: icons and portraits are host-supplied props with a neutral themed placeholder.
- A newly ported family lives in its own `_ak-<family>.scss` partial and its own `src/ak/ui/<family>/Ak*.tsx` file.

### 2.13 Composition recipes

Three starting points. Only verified props appear below; adapt the copy, keep the ratios.

**A. Command deck — `terminal` intensity.** One dominant readout; everything else is context, and
every number must be real. `tone` on `AkCommand` picks a surface tint (`default` / `paper` /
`primary` / `muted` / `dark` / `cyan` / `accent`) — it is not a danger/warning semantic.

```tsx
<AkScreen tone="dark" title="DEPOT" eyebrow="MANAGEMENT // 01" backLabel="RETURN" onBack={close}>
  <AkStatRow>
    <AkStat label="LMD" value="42,000" delta="+1,200" trend="up" />
    <AkStat label="ORUNDUM" value="1,800" />
  </AkStatRow>
  <AkCommandGrid>
    <AkCommand label="OPERATIONS" meta="COMBAT // 01-07" tone="accent" onClick={openCombat} />
    <AkCommand label="SQUAD" meta="FORMATION" tone="primary" onClick={openSquad} />
    <AkCommand label="DEPOT" meta="SUPPLY" tone="cyan" onClick={openDepot} />
  </AkCommandGrid>
  <AkProgress label="SUPPLY LINE" value={72} />
</AkScreen>
```

**B. Editorial update page — `system` intensity, works in `archive`.** Let the rows and the media
carry the page; decoration stays underneath them. One signal colour per view is enough.

```tsx
<AkBreadcrumb items={[{ label: 'HOME', href: '/' }, { label: 'UPDATES' }]} />
<AkHeading level={1}>Operation update</AkHeading>
<AkBilingual cn="作战记录" en="OPERATIONS" row />
<AkNewsList
  label="Site notices"
  empty="No notices yet"
  items={[{ category: 'NOTICE', title: 'Maintenance complete', time: '10-20', dateTime: '2026-10-20', href: '/news/1' }]}
/>
<AkMediaGallery label="Archive" items={items} onValueChange={setIndex} />
```

**C. Settings form — `accent` → `system`.** `AkField` has no `label` prop: the visible label is
`AkFieldLabel` (or `AkInput label`, which sets the accessible name). Errors are text plus signal
colour, never colour alone.

```tsx
<AkFormStack>
  <AkField hint="Shown in the roster" required>
    <AkFieldLabel htmlFor="callsign">CALLSIGN</AkFieldLabel>
    <AkInput id="callsign" defaultValue="Amiya" />
  </AkField>
  <AkField help="Changes the badge colour, not permissions.">
    <AkFieldLabel htmlFor="role">ROLE</AkFieldLabel>
    <AkSelect id="role" defaultValue="caster">
      <option value="caster">Caster</option>
    </AkSelect>
  </AkField>
  <AkChoice checked={notify} onChange={(event) => setNotify(event.target.checked)}>
    Notify on deployment
  </AkChoice>
  <AkButton variant="action" type="submit">Save</AkButton>
</AkFormStack>
```

**Reading order beats symmetry**: primary value → action → context → metadata. If a layout needs a
second focal point, it is probably two screens.


---

## 3. Component Categories & Documentation

### 3.1 Actions & Buttons

#### `AkButton`
Industrial tactile button featuring an animated sweeping light-band highlight on hover, active scale depression, and focus rings.

```tsx
import { AkButton } from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react'

// Variants: 'default' | 'outline' | 'action' | 'advanced' | 'light' | 'danger' | 'ghost'
<AkButton variant="action" icon={<span>◆</span>} onClick={() => deploy()}>
  CONFIRM DEPLOYMENT
</AkButton>

<AkButton variant="outline" block>FULL WIDTH</AkButton>
<AkButton disabled>UNAVAILABLE</AkButton>
```

Props:
- `variant?: 'default' | 'outline' | 'action' | 'advanced' | 'light' | 'danger' | 'ghost'` (default: `'default'`)
- `icon?: ReactNode`: Leading inline icon slot
- `block?: boolean` (default: `false`): Stretches to 100% width
- `disabled?: boolean`: Native disabled state

#### `AkButtonGroup`
Horizontal cluster wrapper with unified borders and segment flow.

```tsx
<AkButtonGroup>
  <AkButton variant="outline">PREV</AkButton>
  <AkButton variant="outline">NEXT</AkButton>
</AkButtonGroup>
```

#### `AkTag` / `AkTagGroup`
Tactical status tags with cut chamfer corners and coloured signal indicators. `AkTag` renders a
static `<span>` by default — it is a label, not a control.

```tsx
import { AkChip, AkTag, AkTagGroup } from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react'

<AkTag variant="advanced">MELEE</AkTag>
<AkTag variant="danger">CROWD CONTROL</AkTag>

// A tag that must toggle renders a real <button>: `as="button"` + aria-pressed.
// Hover, press, disabled and focus-visible come from the stylesheet; selection is aria-pressed.
<AkTag as="button" variant="outline" aria-pressed={filter === 'MELEE'} onClick={() => setFilter('MELEE')}>
  MELEE
</AkTag>

// A grouped checkable filter with an icon slot is AkChip instead.
<AkChip checked={isSelected} onCheckedChange={setSelected}>SURVIVAL</AkChip>
```

---

### 3.2 Menus & Disclosure

Backed by the native browser Popover API. Esc, outside click, and top-layer stacking are handled automatically by the platform.

```tsx
import {
  AkDropdownMenu,
  AkContextMenu,
  AkMenubar,
  AkToolbar,
  AkCollapsible,
  AkMenuGroup,
  AkMenuSeparator,
} from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react'

// Dropdown Menu:
<AkDropdownMenu
  label="TACTICAL MENU"
  items={[
    { label: 'Inspect Sector', onSelect: () => inspect(), shortcut: '⌘I' },
    { label: 'Deploy Squad', onSelect: () => deploy(), shortcut: '⌘D' },
    { label: 'Abort Operation', destructive: true, onSelect: () => abort() }
  ]}
/>

// Context Menu (Right Click):
<AkContextMenu items={[{ label: 'Archive', onSelect: () => archive() }]}>
  <div className="panel">Right click here</div>
</AkContextMenu>

// Menubar & Toolbar:
<AkMenubar aria-label="Editor Menu">
  <button type="button" role="menuitem">FILE</button>
  <button type="button" role="menuitem">EDIT</button>
</AkMenubar>

// Collapsible disclosure:
<AkCollapsible title="OPERATIONAL BRIEFING">
  <p>Target coordinates confirmed.</p>
</AkCollapsible>
```

---

### 3.3 Cards & Surfaces

#### `AkCard`
Layered rectangular panel with structured header, content, and footer slots.

```tsx
import {
  AkCard,
  AkCardHeader,
  AkCardTitle,
  AkCardDescription,
  AkCardContent,
  AkCardFooter,
} from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react'

<AkCard as="article" variant="default">
  <AkCardHeader>
    <AkCardTitle>MISSION 01-07</AkCardTitle>
    <AkCardDescription>Sub-surface Originium veins</AkCardDescription>
  </AkCardHeader>
  <AkCardContent>
    Defend all critical extraction gates.
  </AkCardContent>
  <AkCardFooter>
    <AkButton variant="action">START</AkButton>
  </AkCardFooter>
</AkCard>
```

#### Surface Treatments
- `AkBackdrop`: Matte overlay layer with `strength` ('light' | 'heavy') — no backdrop blur in 2.0
- `AkGrain`: Procedural noise overlay for vast empty dark fields
- `AkMosaic`: Data de-sync pixelation block for corrupted/classified data
- `AkVignette`: Darkened corner gradient pushing visual focus inward
- `AkStripeEdge`: High-visibility left hazard stripe edge

---

### 3.4 Feedback & Status

```tsx
import { AkNotice, AkStatus, AkProgress, AkGauge } from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react'

// Notices with cut corners and technical status code:
<AkNotice title="SYSTEM ALERT" code="PRTS.ERR" variant="danger">
  Catastrophe precursor detected in Sector 4.
</AkNotice>

// Pulse indicator status readout:
<AkStatus label="SYSTEM" detail="Online" />
<AkStatus label="COMMS" detail="Degraded" variant="warning" />

// Progress bars and segmented gauges:
<AkProgress value={75} max={100} label="STABILIZING" />
<AkGauge value={4} max={5} label="DIFFICULTY" />
```

---

### 3.5 Inputs & Form

Dark-terminal native inputs with cyan indicators, monospace labels, and custom switch/radio shapes.

```tsx
import {
  AkFormStack,
  AkField,
  AkFieldLabel,
  AkInput,
  AkSelect,
  AkTextarea,
  AkChoice,
  AkSlider,
  AkInputNumber,
  AkSegmented,
} from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react'

<AkFormStack>
  <AkField hint="ENTER OPERATOR ID">
    <AkFieldLabel htmlFor="op-id">CODE</AkFieldLabel>
    <AkInput id="op-id" placeholder="R001" value={code} onChange={e => setCode(e.target.value)} />
  </AkField>

  <AkField>
    <AkSelect value={role} onChange={e => setRole(e.target.value)}>
      <option value="caster">Caster</option>
      <option value="medic">Medic</option>
    </AkSelect>
  </AkField>

  <AkChoice checked={live} onChange={e => setLive(e.target.checked)}>CHECKLIST CONFIRMED</AkChoice>
  <AkChoice variant="switch" checked={comms} onChange={e => setComms(e.target.checked)}>RADIO LINK</AkChoice>
</AkFormStack>

// Slider & Stepper:
<AkSlider value={volume} onValueChange={setVolume} label="AUDIO GAIN" />
<AkInputNumber value={quantity} onValueChange={setQuantity} min={1} max={99} />
<AkSegmented options={['ALL', 'ELITE 1', 'ELITE 2']} value={stage} onValueChange={setStage} />
```

**Dual-mode state (2.0):** every value control takes either `value` + `onValueChange` (controlled) or
`defaultValue` (uncontrolled). A defined `value` always wins; `onValueChange` fires in both modes.
Disclosure components (`AkDialog`, `AkCollapsible`) use `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange`.

---

### 3.6 Navigation

```tsx
import { AkTabs, AkBreadcrumb } from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react'

<AkTabs
  value={activeTab}
  onValueChange={setActiveTab}
  items={[
    { value: 'ops', label: 'OPERATIONS', title: 'Operations' },
    { value: 'roster', label: 'ROSTER', title: 'Roster' },
  ]}
  renderPanel={(item) => <div>{item.title}</div>}
/>

<AkBreadcrumb
  items={[
    { label: 'RHODES ISLAND', href: '#' },
    { label: 'TERMINAL', href: '#' },
    { label: 'INFRASTRUCTURE' }
  ]}
/>
```

### 3.7 Effects & Depth

Motion language built with CSS animations and Web Animations API controllers:

```tsx
import {
  AkEntrance,
  AkCountUp,
  AkDepth,
  AkDepthLayer,
  AkParticleField,
  AkGlow,
  AkOutline,
  AkSkew,
} from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react'

// Entrance animation controller with replay():
const entranceRef = useRef<AkEntranceHandle>(null)
<AkEntrance ref={entranceRef}>
  <div>Panel animating in on mount</div>
</AkEntrance>
entranceRef.current?.replay()

// Rolling numeric readout:
<AkCountUp value={2048} duration={800} />

// Mouse-tracking 3D parallax depth:
<AkDepth variant="stage" threeD>
  <AkDepthLayer depth={0.4} className="bg-grid" />
  <AkDepthLayer depth={1.0} className="main-content"><AkDisplay xl>PRTS</AkDisplay></AkDepthLayer>
  <AkDepthLayer depth={2.0} className="hud-brackets" />
</AkDepth>

// Tactical micro-effects:
<AkGlow tone="action"><AkButton>BREATHING GLOW</AkButton></AkGlow>
<AkOutline color="#18d1ff"><AkButton>EXPANDING RING</AkButton></AkOutline>
<AkSkew direction="left"><AkInverse>10 DEGREE SKEW</AkInverse></AkSkew>
```

## 4. Tuning Reference — Which Token to Set

Every tuning token below is a real CSS custom property read by the component's stylesheet. Set it
per instance with the `tokens` prop, or globally on `:root` / any scoped selector.

Two entries in the table are CSS-only: `AkFormStack` and `AkProgressStack` do not accept a
`tokens` prop, so override their token through a scoped rule instead. Exact prop names, types and
defaults for every component are in [`docs/api.md`](./docs/api.md).

| Component | Tunable tokens |
| :--- | :--- |
| `AkButton` | `--ak-button-height`, `--ak-button-min-width`, `--ak-button-pad-x`, `--ak-button-fs`, `--ak-button-icon`, `--ak-button-bg`, `--ak-button-fg`, `--ak-button-sheen`, `--ak-button-shadow`, `--ak-button-border` |
| `AkCard` | `--ak-card-pad`, `--ak-card-gap`, `--ak-card-title-fs`, `--ak-card-bg`, `--ak-card-border`, `--ak-card-shadow`, `--ak-card-shadow-hover`, `--ak-card-w`, `--ak-card-h`, `--ak-card-place-color` |
| `AkTag` | `--ak-tag-height`, `--ak-tag-pad`, `--ak-tag-fs`, `--ak-tag-signal`, `--ak-tag-text`, `--ak-tag-surface`, `--ak-cut` |
| `AkStatus` | `--ak-status-sig`, `--ak-status-min-h`, `--ak-status-pad`, `--ak-status-label-fs`, `--ak-status-detail-fs`, `--ak-status-signal`, `--ak-shadow-signal` |
| `AkInput` / `AkTextarea` / `AkSelect` | `--ak-field-min-h`, `--ak-field-pad`, `--ak-field-fs`, `--ak-field-signal`, `--ak-select-arrow-x` |
| `AkProgress` | `--ak-progress-pad`, `--ak-progress-track-h`, `--ak-progress-fs`, `--ak-progress-gap`, `--ak-progress-bg`, `--ak-progress-signal` |
| `AkGauge` | `--ak-gauge-w`, `--ak-gauge-value-fs`, `--ak-gauge-inset`, `--ak-gauge-hole`, `--ak-gauge-signal` |
| `AkTable` | `--ak-table-pad-y`, `--ak-table-pad-x`, `--ak-table-fs`, `--ak-table-width` |
| `AkDialog` | `--ak-dialog-w`, `--ak-dialog-max-h`, `--ak-dialog-pad`, `--ak-dialog-fs`, `--ak-dialog-bg`, `--ak-dialog-fg`, `--ak-dialog-body-fg`, `--ak-dialog-border`, `--ak-dialog-shadow`, `--ak-cut` |
| `AkTabs` | `--ak-tabs-tab-h`, `--ak-tabs-tab-pad`, `--ak-tabs-tab-fs`, `--ak-tabs-panel-pad`, `--ak-tabs-width`, `--ak-tabs-signal` |
| `AkSegmented` | `--ak-segmented-item-w`, `--ak-segmented-item-h`, `--ak-segmented-item-pad`, `--ak-segmented-fs`, `--ak-segmented-inset`, `--ak-segmented-bg`, `--ak-segmented-signal` |
| `AkPagination` | `--ak-pagination-h`, `--ak-pagination-w`, `--ak-pagination-arrow-w`, `--ak-pagination-number-fs`, `--ak-pagination-title-fs`, `--ak-pagination-bg`, `--ak-pagination-fg`, `--ak-pagination-arrow-bg`, `--ak-pagination-arrow-bg-hover`, `--ak-pagination-arrow-bg-disabled`, `--ak-pagination-cur-border` |
| `AkDropdownMenu` / `AkContextMenu` | `--ak-menu-trigger-h`, `--ak-menu-trigger-pad`, `--ak-menu-trigger-fs`, `--ak-menu-item-h`, `--ak-menu-item-pad`, `--ak-menu-item-fs`, `--ak-menu-min-w`, `--ak-menu-max-w` |
| `AkPopover` / tooltip | `--ak-popover-w`, `--ak-popover-pad`, `--ak-popover-title-fs`, `--ak-popover-body-fs`, `--ak-popover-eyebrow-fs`, `--ak-popover-bg`, `--ak-popover-fg`, `--ak-popover-title-fg`, `--ak-popover-body-fg`, `--ak-popover-border`, `--ak-popover-shadow`, `--ak-tooltip-max-w`, `--ak-tooltip-pad`, `--ak-tooltip-fs` |
| any form group | `--ak-form-w` (form stack max width — CSS only, `AkFormStack` has no `tokens` prop) |
| any progress group | `--ak-progress-stack-w` (CSS only, `AkProgressStack` has no `tokens` prop) |

Global: `--ak-density-scale` (spacing), `--ak-density-control` (control heights). Prefer `data-ak-density` over setting these by hand.

---

## 5. Subpath Exports & Controllers

Framework-agnostic controllers are accessible via subpaths without React dependencies. Each one has
a React wrapper in the main entry — prefer the wrapper unless you are driving a non-React surface.

```ts
import { createSectionNavigation, createMobileMenu, createMediaGallery, createAssetLoader, createParticleField } from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react/core'
import { createCountUp, createEntrance } from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react/core/effects'
import { createDashboardDepth } from '@swufefox/ak-ui-react/core/depth'
```

| Controller | React wrapper | Returns |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `createSectionNavigation(root, options)` | `AkSectionNavigator` | `navigate(id, { history, focus, immediate })`, `currentId`, `destroy()` — native wheel/touch scrolling, hash/history sync, interruptible |
| `createMobileMenu(dialog, { trigger })` | `AkMobileMenu` | `open()`, `close()`, `isOpen`, `destroy()` — native `<dialog>` owns focus trapping and Escape; the controller owns the 200ms / 70ms stagger |
| `createMediaGallery(root, options)` | `AkMediaGallery` | `select(index, { focus, animate })`, `refresh()`, `open()`, `close()`, `index`, `destroy()` |
| `createAssetLoader(onChange)` | `AkAssetLoader` | `load(tasks)`, `cancel()`, `destroy()` — tasks receive an `AbortSignal`; progress counts settled tasks, not bytes |
| `createParticleField(canvas, options)` | `AkParticleField` | `setPattern()`, `pause()`, `resume()`, `renderer`, `destroy()` — WebGL → 2D → static fallback |
| `createEntrance(element, options)` | `AkEntrance` | `play()`, `cancel()`, `destroy()` |
| `createCountUp(render, options)` | `AkCountUp` | `play()`, `update(value)`, `finish()`, `destroy()` |
| `createDashboardDepth(root, options)` | `AkDepth` | `destroy()` — writes `--ak-layer-x` / `--ak-layer-y` on `[data-depth]` layers |

Controller contract: create it after the element is attached to the document, keep the instance in
a ref, and call `destroy()` on unmount. Creating a controller never starts an animation — call
`play()` on the intended event. Never create one during render. Full signatures and option types
are in [`docs/api.md`](./docs/api.md).

---

## 6. Summary of Common Mistakes to Avoid

| Anti-pattern | Recommended Pattern | Reason |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Inline `style={{ height: '2.25rem' }}` to shrink a control | `size="sm"`, or `tokens={{ '--ak-button-height': '2.25rem' }}` | Inline styles bypass the density/tier system and drift out of sync across the app |
| Round avatars (`border-radius: 50%`) | Rectangular or chamfer cut avatars (`<AkAvatar cut />`) | Arknights design language strictly forbids bubbly round cards/avatars |
| Hardcoded `#fff` or `#000` colors | `var(--ak-text-primary)`, `var(--ak-surface-canvas)` | Breaks theme inversion between Terminal (dark) and Archive (light) |
| Fixed widths on buttons (`width: 150px`) | `min-width: 120px; width: auto;` (built into `AkButton`) | Avoids text clipping on longer phrases and CJK/English labels |
| Hand-rolled CSS diagonal stripes | `<AkStripes variant="hazard" />` or `<AkGridBackdrop />` | Reuses canonical vector-math SVG/CSS tokens across the system |
| Generic spinner icons | `<AkSpinner />` | Retains Arknights 45-degree rotating diamond radio-wave indicator |
| Unstyled tooltips/popovers sticking out on mobile | `<AkPopover />` | Built-in `min(calc(100vw - 32px), ...)` prevents mobile viewport blowout |

---

## 7. Sources

- **ak-ui** — https://github.com/YunYouJun/ak-ui (Vue + CSS core). The design contract in section 2 is the React port of the upstream `skills/ak-ui` package: `SKILL.md` plus the `design-language`, `tokens`, `motion`, `headless-components`, `site` and `quality-checklist` references. The stylesheet, tokens and DOM controllers in this package are vendored from it.
- **prts-design** — https://github.com/MooncellWiki/prts-design (MIT). Source of the Arknights data layers, the decor language, the panel/feedback families and the border, sunken-surface and rarity tokens; see section 2.12 for the porting rules.
- **This package** — [`docs/api.md`](./docs/api.md) for every prop, variant and method; `AGENTS.md` for architecture and contribution rules; https://ak-ui-react.pages.dev for live previews and copyable examples.
